text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT triggered: KV_CACHE_EVICT_RATE > 5% over 3m for service:inference-runtime (monitor id: DD-9523). Auto-paging oncall.

Miguel (eng-oncall): i'm on it. seeing spike in eviction rate and corresponding tail latency bump. paging chris and amy.

Amy (eng-sre): ack. grabbing logs and dashboards. any initial customer-facing impact?

Miguel (eng-oncall): some customer requests hitting fallback model (gold->silver) according to routing logs. Not widespread but we have a few active requests with timeout retries -> 500s.

Chris (eng-runtime): thanks. looking at runtime metrics — KV cache hit rate dropping from ~92% -> 60% over last 6m. eviction pressure coming from a hot sharded namespace. suspect noisy job or regression in prefix caching.

Samantha (prod-obs): seeing alert noise from the old eviction monitor. it's firing for small blips too. can we suppress duplicates while we triage? :eyes:

Miguel (eng-oncall): @DevEx Bot can you mute monitor DD-9523 for 10m and suppress duplicates?

DevEx Bot: executed: monitor DD-9523 muted for 10 minutes by Miguel. suppress_duplicates=true.

Amy (eng-sre): mitigation plan: 1) identify offending tenant(s) causing eviction storm 2) increase eviction threshold temporarily 3) add short-term routing to a less-sensitive cache tier or increase cache size for affected pool.

Chris (eng-runtime): running a query to see top keys by eviction count:

```
# prometheus-ish pseudo query
topk(10, sum by(cache_key)(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="inference"}[5m])))
```

Chris (eng-runtime): top offenders: tenant:acme-search (38% of evicts), tenant:beta-payments (22%). acme-search has a misbehaving batch job that blasts prefixes.

Amy (eng-sre): created a temporary iptables QoS rule to throttle that job's workers in the dedicated pool to reduce thrash. Applying now.

Miguel (eng-oncall): applied. monitoring immediate effect.

Samantha (prod-obs): after throttle, eviction rate dropping. KV hit rate climbing back to ~85% in the last 2m. tail latency falling.

Chris (eng-runtime): good. but long-term we need better alerts / dashboards. current eviction monitor was simple threshold on evict rate; it floods on transient noise. we should tune to sustained evictions and correlate with hit-rate and fallback_count.

Amy (eng-sre): agreed. propose new monitor expression (Datadog style) to reduce noise and catch sustained issues:

```
# datadog monitor: sustained_kv_eviction
(avg(last_5m):avg:kv_cache.eviction_rate{service:inference} by {pool} > 0.05) && (avg(last_5m):avg:kv_cache.hit_rate{service:inference} by {pool} < 0.8)
```

Amy (eng-sre): also add recovery condition and a 3m no-data handling to avoid flapping.

Chris (eng-runtime): I'll add a per-tenant alert for sudden eviction bursts using rate-of-change and a guardrail to exclude known maintenance windows.

Samantha (prod-obs): can we create a dashboard tile that shows: hit rate, eviction rate, fallback_count, and top 10 eviction-causing keys over 1h? that'll speed future triage.

Miguel (eng-oncall): agreed. I'll create the dashboard and add it to the oncall runbook.

Chris (eng-runtime): created a quick dashboard: /dashboards/kv-cache-ops (sharing link)

Miguel (eng-oncall): adding runbook steps: 1) check dashboard -> top keys 2) if single-tenant >30% evicts, contact infra on that tenant and apply throttle 3) if multi-tenant thrash, scale cache pool or enable temporary pinning to fast tier 4) if fallback_count > 1% for >10m, page SEV2.

Amy (eng-sre): i'm going to update the alert definition now. changing alert sensitivity and adding tags to avoid cross-environment storms:

```
# new alert proto (examples)
name: "sustained-kv-eviction-v2"
expr: "increase(kv_cache_evictions_total{env:prod}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{env:prod}[10m]) > 0.05"
for: 6m
labels: {severity: "warn", team: "eng-runtime"}
annotations: {runbook: "/runbooks/kv-eviction"}
```

Amy (eng-sre): pushed change to Datadog/Grafana. monitor id: DD-9523 -> replaced by DD-9601.

DevEx Bot: monitor DD-9601 created and linked. CI config: dashboards/kv-cache-ops.json updated.

Samantha (prod-obs): note: we should also create an eviction alert for rapid spikes (for SEV1 potential) that considers fallback_count and 95th latency. I'll add that as a separate monitor.

Miguel (eng-oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem: ~12 requests experienced fallback model and 3 customers reported increased latency. mitigation prevented broader impact. incident window ~ 1834001234 -> 1834004234 (about 50m).

Chris (eng-runtime): root cause: noisy tenant job (acme-search) causing key churn and eviction storm. Fix PR requested on tenant side to use TTLs and prefixing. we've also added a server-side temporary pin for hot prefixes.

Amy (eng-sre): action items (assigned):
- Amy: finalize new monitor DD-9601 and add mute rules for maintenance windows. (ETA: today)
- Chris: implement per-tenant eviction-rate monitor and automate throttling playbook. (ETA: 2 days)
- Miguel: add kv-cache-ops dashboard to oncall runbook + update runbook steps. (ETA: today)
- Samantha: write post-incident note and customer impact blurb for support to use. (ETA: EOD)

Miguel (eng-oncall): handing off to daytime oncall @Amy. I'm leaving notes in the thread. :raised_hands:

Amy (eng-sre): taking over. will watch alerts for 2 hours. please ping if anything else pops up.

Chris (eng-runtime): follow-up: i'll also add a histogram tile for eviction TTL distribution; we can detect pathological low-TTL patterns earlier.

Samantha (prod-obs): postmortem checklist: include timeline, metrics, mitigations, alert tuning diffs (old->new alert expressions), dashboard screenshots, and customer communication draft.

Miguel (eng-oncall): thanks team. good quick coordination. closing this thread once postmortem doc is up.

DevEx Bot: incident thread marked resolved by Amy (eng-sre).
